summary_responses.response: This paper introduces DiffTry (Differential Retries), a lightweight mechanism that addresses the problem of microservice overload, where independently auto-scaled services can become miscoordinated and reject valuable high-priority transactions—especially during traffic spikes or adversarial overload attacks. Traditional retries fail in these situations because they treat all requests equally, failing to protect valuable transactions and potentially triggering performance-degrading "retry storms." DiffTry solves this by assigning class-specific retry-attempt limits (e.g., more retries for premium users, fewer for low-priority traffic), effectively transforming retries into a distributed rejection-prioritization mechanism that requires no overload sensing, service coordination, or application changes. The authors develop an analytical framework—covering a single overloaded service and general service networks—that lets practitioners predict per-class rejection rates, with formal guarantees including convergence of the solution, uniqueness for DAG-based transaction flows, and monotonic improvement of success rates as retry limits increase. The model's predictions were validated both in simulation and on a live Kubernetes deployment as a drop-in service-mesh plugin, where measured rejection rates closely matched the theoretical analysis, showing that high-priority transactions can capture the large majority of successful completions even under heavy load.

summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) has issued a direct final rule making technical revisions to its Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations to incorporate statutory amendments from January 2021 and December 2023. The rule expands FMLA eligibility by counting virtually all Federal civilian service, including temporary and intermittent employment, as well as certain honorable active military service, toward the 12-month qualifying service requirement. It also clarifies that annual and sick leave earned under authorities outside of title 5, United States Code, may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave. Additionally, the rule excludes certain Veterans Health Administration (VHA) employees covered under a separate leave system from title 5 FMLA coverage. The rule takes effect December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026, in which case OPM will withdraw the affected provisions and issue a proposed rulemaking.
